Subject: Post-call: isolation requirements & hosting options for PulseCare

Hi Ava — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the follow-ups we discussed so we have alignment on next steps.

What I heard (high level):
- PulseCare will be processing regulated health data (PHI) for real-time triage and symptom-check flows.
- Primary concern: noisy-neighbor risk and data isolation for model inputs/outputs.
- Target latency SLOs: P95 <= 150ms for single-turn inference; P99 under 300ms for strict flows.
- Typical steady-state concurrency: ~120 qps with burst peaks up to ~400 qps during morning surge.
- Compliance ask: need SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration, and contract language for HIPAA BAA.

Hosting options we briefly discussed (options we can support):
- Hosted API (fastest start) — good for lower risk workloads or non-PHI but requires controls/contracting for PHI use.
- Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool; predictable performance and stronger isolation guarantees than shared hosted.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) — full isolation, customer-managed networking; best for strict regulatory requirements.

Open questions / asks from our side to vendor/procurement (helps scope recommendation):
1) Can you confirm whether all inference payloads will be PHI (yes/no/partial)?
2) Expected average and peak qps per region and whether burst behavior is predictable by schedule.
3) Any hard constraints on where keys are stored (customer KMS / HSM requirement)?
4) Procurement timeline and whether you need a vendor questionnaire completed this week.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short isolation_requirements_summary.pdf that maps options to risk levels + our recommended PoC. Please send your SOC2 questionnaire (or procurement doc) and I’ll loop in our security lead.

Next steps I propose:
- You send SOC2 checklist + confirmation on PHI scope (Ava) — target: Tue 10/27
- We provide short architecture note and PoC plan (Ben) — target: Thu 10/29
- If Private/Dedicated looks necessary, schedule a technical workshop next week to nail network/keys.

Thanks again — I’ll keep this short.

Thanks Jordan — great summary. Quick answers and a couple clarifications below.

1) PHI scope: yes, all inference payloads for triage flows are PHI. Non-sensitive analytics events are separate and can be routed differently.
2) Traffic profile: steady-state ~120 qps US-east; peaks ~350–420 qps in the morning window (06:00–09:30 ET). Bursts are tied to scheduled notifications and are reasonably predictable.
3) Keys: must be customer-controlled KMS for decryption of patient identifiers; we can discuss HSM on a later call.
4) Timeline: procurement is aggressive — pricing and architecture recommendation required to close budget by mid-November. Procurement will send the vendor security questionnaire; I attached the first pass (PulseCare_SOC2_Questionnaire_v2.docx).

Preferred path: Our security team prefers Dedicated capacity or Private VPC for core inference (the hosted shared tier is a non-starter for PHI). The critical ask is a documented blast-radius/tenancy explanation and how you meet P99 latency guarantees under burst.

Happy to jump on a technical workshop this week. Suggested times: Wed 10/28 10:00–11:00 ET or Thu 10/29 14:00–15:00 ET.

-Ava

Ava / Jordan — thanks, and appreciate the details in the questionnaire. High-level proposal below; attaching a one-page deployment_blueprint and a short cost sketch.

Recommendation (short):
- Primary: Dedicated capacity in customer-owned VPC (Dedicated + VPC peering) for phase 1 PoC. This gives predictable GPU isolation (no noisy-neighbor on the same pool) while letting PulseCare keep network/KMS control.
- Secondary: Offer a Private on-prem deployment as an option if PulseCare requires full air-gapped or on-prem hardware (longer lead time and capex).

How we mitigate noisy-neighbor risk on Dedicated:
- Physical isolation: reserved GPU hosts for your tenancy during the Dedicated pool (guaranteed node reservation).
- Runtime hard isolation: container + network namespace + dedicated inference processes with KV cache scoped to tenant.
- Preemptive autoscaling and burst queueing policies that spin up reserved burst nodes ahead of expected windows; fallback plan to a compatible model variant with graceful latency/cost tradeoff if capacity is exhausted.

Performance SLOs and validation approach:
- PoC goal: demonstrate P95 <= 150ms and P99 <= 300ms for triage model at 120 qps steady with a 400 qps burst test using synthetic traffic.
- Validation: step-load tests, cold-start/long-tail spike tests, and KV-prefix-cache effectiveness measurement.

KMS & key control:
- Support for customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS & CloudHSM) with RBAC and audit logs. For Private on-prem we can integrate with your HSMs (network permitting).

2-week PoC prerequisites (high level):
- PulseCare: test dataset (anonymized / synthetically replayed traffic) + customer KMS access in a staging account.
- Redwood: pre-provisioned dedicated GPU pool + monitoring and SLO dashboard access.
- Security: brief onboarding call with your security engineer to confirm network rules and audit expectations.

Deliverables for PoC (2 weeks):
1) Deployment blueprint and runbook (attachment)
2) Load/latency report with SLO pass/fail and regression baseline
3) Short ops playbook for autoscaling and fallback behavior
4) Ballpark dedicated vs private pricing for a 12-month commit

Workshop: Wed 10/28 10:00 ET works — I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda and the test-plan steps.
